title: cairn outline writes the joined outline with every open question in it
intention: cairn codemother outline writes the requirements pieces joined into one file, followed by an open-questions section, so every unresolved question is visible from that one file: under its Q# at its outline section, or in full when it has no number, and flagged when its Q# has no marker in the outline.
why: Akien 2026-11-17: the joined outline is "the ideal surface for me to field questions from". Measured the same day: outline_bytes joins the pieces only in memory, no command writes them, and 9 of 25 open questions cannot be found from the outline.
traces_to: Law 1 (his answers are the novel input; one surface stops him re-deriving where a question stands); outline 0.6 (a question is placed at the line it bears on).
how: joined.py beside outline_check: join(folder, qroot) = outline_bytes + the questions section; write(out) writes it. cairn/devices/codemother/bin/outline registers it as 'cairn codemother outline' (default ~/.akien/temp/outline.md). Notes give four records their Q#; markers Q#120-Q#123 place four more; 0.6's next number becomes 124.

clauses.claim: cairn codemother outline <out> writes the pieces joined exactly as outline_bytes joins them, followed by an open-questions section, and prints the path it wrote

over a scratch questions corpus, a numbered open question is listed under its Q# with the section its marker stands at, an unnumbered one is listed with its full text, an answered one is not listed, and an open Q# with no marker in the outline is flagged
over the live corpus, every unresolved question id under CairnCommons/questions appears in the joined file
every live unresolved question carries a Q#, and each such Q# has a marker in the pieces unless the section flags it answered in the outline

decisions.text: D1: joined.py reuses outline_check.outline_bytes and cairn.tools.question.list_open. A record's Q# is read from its latest note matching 'outline: Q#n' first, else from 'Q#n (' at the opening or 'where Q#n stands open', never from quoted text. The section groups records by Q# (one entry per Q#, listing its record ids and tickets, its marker's section from the pieces); records without a Q# follow with full text; a Q# with no marker is flagged 'no marker in the outline: answered there? close it'.

D2: cairn/devices/codemother/bin/outline is the shortcut, in the bin of the device it belongs to (outline 5.4.3.7: repo-root bin/ holds only the launcher), so the verb is 'cairn codemother outline'; it copies bin/cmd/outlinecheck's interpreter resolution and runs joined.py with an optional output path, default ~/.akien/temp/outline.md. The outline_check charter's public_interface names 'cairn codemother outline [<out>]'.

D3: markers placed as child lines: Q#120 under 1.3.7.1 (open-6712e6ffac8f), Q#121 under 4.3.1.5.1.6.11 (open-cddfd983ccbc), Q#122 under 6.3.5 (open-a2b93a9882ea), Q#123 under 10.3.11 (open-c9643e21c368); 0.6's next number becomes 124. Notes name the Q# on open-49fc67a40ede (Q#101), open-212b2de5c6b8 (Q#103), open-583a63c6f57a (Q#106), open-fb6c36c5287e (Q#107) and the four new ones.
D4: the proof, one tooth per clause; tooth 2 over a scratch commons and scratch pieces.

out: back-propagating Akien's edits of the joined file into the pieces (CC's hand for now, by his word)

measured.saw: 25 unresolved questions; 16 name a Q# whose marker stands; 4 sit at a marker their text never names; 4 unplaced; 1 (Q#105) answered at 11.3.5.1.1 but still open; no bin/cmd verb writes the joined outline
measured.how: a script over CairnCommons/questions/open-*.json against grep '\[Q#' of the pieces; ls bin/cmd
